header:
Date: 2025-03-21
Time: 16:00 PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Reyes (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marcus Lee (BlueCove Head of Platform), Nadia Ortega (BlueCove SRE), Kareem Aziz (BlueCove CTO)
summary: Weekly POC sync focusing on staging access, credential handoff, and SLO targets. Customer confirmed they could provision a peered staging VPC but need a dry-run plan for canary traffic and KMS integration details. SE requested a short latency benchmarking run with the provided script. Action items assigned around SOC2 docs, bench runs, and scheduling a canary dry-run.
topics: staging VPC peering and bastion access
canary traffic dry-run and rollback plan
dedicated vs hosted economics for sustained 1k rps
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Reyes: all right everyone uh thanks for joining, let's try to keep this to 45 and get the staging gate closed today
[00:18] Marcus Lee: yeah sounds good, we just came from an internal where we're trying to get the VPC peering in, so status is almost there, Nadia has the subnet ranges, we just need the Redwood inbound rule list
[00:36] Nadia Ortega: yeah i've created the ticket, I'm waiting on a couple of firewall exceptions, one note, our security team wants to use our KMS for at-rest keying, so we need the guide for envelope flow
[00:54] Priya Nair: that's fine, we have a KMS integration document and an HSM note, Jordan will drop the links; technically Redwood supports both customer-managed KMS and our key wrap approach, there can be a small perf hit if you use customer KMS on every token but we typically recommend envelope with a short-lived wrapping key
[01:12] Kareem Aziz: what kind of perf hit are we talking, ballpark? because for our user flows p95 is pretty tight
[01:30] Priya Nair: fair question, for customer KMS per-request it's small but variable, typical extra latency 5-15ms if you're doing a roundtrip to cloud KMS; we avoid that by caching the wrapped key for the session and then only rotate on boundary events, that drops it to near-zero overhead
[01:48] Jordan Reyes: i'll include best-practice config, and note the default TTLs. also i'll attach the SOC2 summary we usually send to customers for compliance review
[02:06] Marcus Lee: excellent. on the bench, what do you want us to run? we have a mixed text generation workload and an embeddings batch job overnight
[02:24] Priya Nair: we prepared a short bench script — it runs a 1k rps mixed traffic profile for one hour but with smaller warmup; we'll provide a sample payload for your typical prompt, and measure p50/p95/p99, plus GPU utilization and token cost estimate
[02:42] Nadia Ortega: can you share that in the next 24 hours? we can run it in staging once peering is in
[02:58] Priya Nair: yes, i'll put that in the repo, Jordan will share the link
[03:16] Jordan Reyes: note, for the canary dry-run, we recommend a stepped traffic profile — start with 1% production, hold for 15 minutes, check SLOs, then 5%, 20% then full cut if green. we also suggest a fallback to a cheaper quantized variant if latency spikes
[03:34] Kareem Aziz: cheaper model variants ok, do you have quant profiles? our product team worries about quality regression
[03:52] Priya Nair: we do. Redwood Optimize will recommend a quant profile per workload; we can pair quant configs with prompt sets and evaluate quality with a small eval harness. we can do a quick A/B on most-critical prompt set during the dry-run
[04:10] Marcus Lee: perfect. security question — SSO and RBAC, we need SAML and SCIM support for our product org, and audit logs retention for 1 year
[04:28] Jordan Reyes: SAML + SCIM is supported, and audit logs can be exported to your SIEM; retention tiers are a paid add-on but we can supply a retention schedule and sample syslog/elk export formats
[04:46] Nadia Ortega: great, also want to confirm network egress — do we need static IPs for firewall allowlist?
[05:04] Priya Nair: for hosted we have egress ranges, for Dedicated we can provide static egress IPs or private connectivity. for pilot you can use the hosted IP ranges but if you want deterministic egress for compliance, Dedicated or VPC peering is recommended
[05:22] Marcus Lee: understood. cost question: Dedicated capacity versus Hosted for sustained 1k rps — we'd prefer not to overcommit initially
[05:40] Jordan Reyes: we can model cost both ways; hosted gives easier start, Dedicated gives predictability — Jordan will send a short TCO note with commitment breakpoints and when Dedicated makes sense vs aggressive autoscale on hosted
[05:58] Kareem Aziz: on the bench data, what are you measuring for tokenization differences? we saw earlier differences in token counts between two open models and it skewed cost
[06:16] Priya Nair: good call — bench script will include tokenizer checks across model variants and output token counts; we also keep a conversion table in the report so you can normalize cost estimates
[06:34] Marcus Lee: timeline: we ideally want a low-risk canary the week of 31st, is that feasible?
[06:52] Jordan Reyes: yes, if peering and creds are done by 26th we can do the dry-run on 31st. action items are aligned to that date
[07:10] Nadia Ortega: one snag — our security asked for an architecture diagram that shows data flow for DeeP logs, can you produce that? they want to see PII boundaries and where logs live
[07:28] Priya Nair: we have a standard architecture doc. i'll annotate it with your PII boundaries and show how we redact request bodies in logs and how audit events are emitted
[07:46] Marcus Lee: can you also call out where KV cache keys live? our SRE is worried about sensitive key material
[08:04] Priya Nair: yes, KV cache is ephemeral in memory on the serving node, and keys are not persisted in plaintext. if you're using customer KMS we never persist plaintext keys; envelope keys are rotated and cached in memory only
[08:22] Jordan Reyes: quick note on rollback: our runtime supports immediate fallback to a smaller model or to a regional replica; we can script an automated fallback but it's a bit of ops work in your infra, or we can provide a managed fallback policy in Dedicated
[08:40] Kareem Aziz: how does that integrate with our canary metrics? can we set automatic thresholds?
[08:58] Priya Nair: yes, the canary orchestration looks at p95 and error rate; thresholds are configurable — we can default to p95 > 200ms or error rate > 2% to trigger rollback, but we'll tune to your baselines
[09:16] Marcus Lee: sample metrics we'll check: p50, p95, p99, token throughput, GPU util, errors/sec, and request tail latency
[09:34] Jordan Reyes: speaking of errors, we saw a customer with a KV cache miss storm on their first pilot because TTLs were too low. tip — we'll recommend TTLs based on your prompt shape. Priya will send suggested defaults
[09:52] Priya Nair: yes sent as part of the bench notes; also include batching configs — continuous batching vs fixed batch can change latency/cost tradeoffs
[10:10] Nadia Ortega: is there any manual step to enable continuous batching?
[10:28] Priya Nair: it's runtime-level config, we set batching policy per route. you can tune max wait and max batch tokens. we'll help pick defaults for your traffic pattern
[10:46] Jordan Reyes: okay quick check, who's taking which next step? Marcus you will confirm success criteria, Nadia provisioning peering, Jordan to send docs and bench script, Priya will help with bench + arch diagrams
[11:04] Marcus Lee: yep i'll sync org and post criteria by next Tue
[11:22] Nadia Ortega: i'll spin up the peer and share a minimal bastion user and ip allowlist by Thursday
[11:40] Priya Nair: we'll also help you instrument a small eval harness to run during the dry-run to check quality; suggest 50-100 critical prompts for A/B
[11:58] Kareem Aziz: that works. last question, are there any compliance caveats for EU data residency if we route to a US region?
[12:16] Jordan Reyes: EU residency is supported with Private deployment or regional hosted endpoints; for pilot we can route to eu-west if you want and keep logs in-region — we'll note that in the SOC2 packet
[12:34] Marcus Lee: good, can you include a brief on data residency options in the email?
[12:52] Jordan Reyes: yes will do. ok let's recap and close
[13:10] Jordan Reyes: recap: Jordan share SOC2 + KMS guide + bench script, Priya provide arch plus bench help, Nadia provision peering, Marcus confirm success criteria. target dry-run 2025-03-31. any objections?
[13:30] Nadia Ortega: none from me
[13:48] Marcus Lee: good to go
[14:06] Kareem Aziz: thanks everyone, appreciate the short checklist
[14:24] Jordan Reyes: thanks all, we'll follow up in email with links and proposed calendar for the dry-run
[14:42] (call ends)
